name: Singleton Reductions Preserve Corner-Peelability Exactly
statement: If an ample one-coordinate expansion $X$ has contraction $A$ and singleton reduction $\{a\}$, then $X$ is corner-peelable if and only if $A$ is corner-peelable. Hence no active singleton-reduction expansion is an ample forbidden pc-minor. Moreover, an untouched component in the opposite layer is not sufficient for forbiddenness: a separated repair over the negative 577-concept double gives a corner-peelable 579-concept lift.
proof: The components of $A-a$, after restoring $a$, occupy disjoint coordinate blocks and attach to the two ends of the sole new-direction edge. If $A$ peels, all component pieces peel and at most one fails to peel to $a$. Peel all other pieces to their attachment vertices, remove the resulting pendant endpoint, and peel the exceptional piece; the converse follows by contraction closure. In the explicit separated repair, peel the repaired first rooted block to zero, delete zero as a leaf across the new edge, and peel the second block.
